column1: # Method batch: ui.Widget (UI base class) + ui.Label.
# First batch of the ui package (86% obfuscated): Widget is the root of the widget hierarchy, so
# naming it clarifies every subclass and every call site in screen/ and ui/hud/.
#   * geometry  - Widget.a(float,float) is the hit test: f1 >= c && f2 >= d && f1 < c+e && f2 < d+f,
#                 i.e. (c,d) = position and (e,f) = size. Container.pack() then confirms it by
#                 computing its own extent as h()+j() (x+width) and i()+k() (y+height).
#   * visibility- Container skips children for which g() is false in BOTH pack() and draw(), and
#                 gates input dispatch on it. Button additionally gates its hit test on g() and
#                 keeps its own DISABLED state, so g() is "visible" and not "enabled".
#                 The constructor sets a_(true) (widgets start visible) and Widget.draw() only
#                 delegates when that flag is set.
#   * color     - the int is handed to SpriteBatch.draw as its last argument, and
#   * data      - listeners read it as an action id: "(Integer)widget.f()" in ListBoxListener,
#                 SquadBarListener, handleWidgetAction(...); MultiplayerLobbyScreen stores a whole
#                 MatchRecord in it, so it is generic user data.
#   * pack()    - Label computes its own size from the text, Button from its style, Container from
#                 the extents of its visible children; it is called after every content change.
#   * input     - Button turns the boolean into PRESSED/HOVER and fires actionListener.onAction(this)
#                 when released; Container forwards with translated coordinates.
# Rows left BLANK on purpose (see 26: keep the trailing tab, they stay 5-column):
#   Label.a(I)          - pure delegate to the inherited setColor(int); naming it setColor would
#                         rewrite its own body into a recursive call.
#   Label.a(ActionListener,FFZ) and Label.a(SpriteBatch,FF) - overrides of the Widget methods
#                         mapped below; the renamer carries the whole override family.
# Descriptors come from javap: do not edit them, the renamer matches on them.
# Columns: owner <TAB> kind <TAB> old <TAB> descriptor <TAB> new
